summary.name: BookStack
summary.one_liner: BookStack is a simple, open-source, self-hosted wiki platform for organising and storing information as books, chapters and pages.
use_cases: Organising internal knowledge base in books and chapters
Writing docs with WYSIWYG or Markdown editors
Restricting wiki access with roles and permissions
Running a wiki with SSO via OIDC, SAML2 or LDAP
summary.what_it_does: BookStack organises content into three levels: books, chapters and pages. Pages can be edited with a WYSIWYG editor or an optional live-preview Markdown editor, and include built-in diagrams.net drawing. Content is searchable at book level or across everything, and any paragraph can be linked directly. It offers page revisions, image management, cross-book sorting, and a full role and permission system. Authentication includes email/password, OIDC, SAML2, LDAP and social logins, with optional MFA (TOTP and backup codes) enforceable per role. The interface supports light and dark themes and multiple languages.
notable: Organises content as books, chapters and pages in a book-like structure
Built-in diagrams.net drawing in the page editor
Supports OIDC, SAML2 and LDAP authentication plus optional MFA
Runs on modest hardware, stated to work on a £2.50 IONOS VPS
caveats: Self-hosting required; the page describes no hosted version
Demo instance restricts user deletion, user updates and setting updates
Listed sponsor services are not tested, vetted or supported by the official project
